items.note: Eight-row schedule, net change (JV+RG)x independent of scratch, intersection coefficients in both constructions and the three-stage composition to (-Y_a,X_a) all follow the proof at 741-765. Neighbour and wire counts (767-782) are not given, but they are not needed for the lemma itself.
States D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1} and the per-route operator with sign. Proves it as the paper does: an invariant at sources, along edges and through gates, using linearity.

The statement is right: nested nondegenerate labels in F^{⊗3}, the budget Wm-2N+2L, losses only on central 3->4 edges of h, and ratios 100/539 and 101/539. The derivation gives the bilinear forms, terminal labels, side-wire inclusion, telescoping and orthonormal bases. It omits the stage transitions and the gate-label table (eq:motif-labels), with central wires going from A⊗F to B⊗F, and the residual table. Those are what show the only decrease is at center 3->4; S1.3.3.4 just quotes that conclusion.

Covers the projection assignment with -P_{U_a} at the X_a sources, rank = dimension change for nested labels, the N exceptional 2P_{U_a} edges, s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b with deficit N-2L_b, and the endpoint identity I_m. This is exactly the proof at 1156-1172.

Edge factorization (weight additive mod 4 under orthogonality, odd weight, Hadamard conjugation to aI+bX_v) and the count s_c with deficit 2N-2L_c follow 1232-1260. The endpoint half is missing. That half computes q_F=wt and q_{U_a^perp}-q_{U_a}=wt+2[u·x], which puts C^{-1} on the 27 support coordinates, and then uses C=iZC^{-1}Z. S1.5.1.5 only names the Z signs and i^{27f} without this reason.
Gives L<N/2, both deficits, eta_b=339/22587335000000 and eta_c=73/19906842167500 above 20·2^{-50}, log m<20, and the exponential inequality giving s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, as at 1319-1344.
Both lemmas are stated with their content. S1.2 also names the split-at-Q-a mechanism of 576-580, but the elementary operations are only quoted, so the item counts as stated.

Elimination from the topmost row and rightmost pivot gives E_1 Pi E_2. Triangular factors are linear-time controlled updates in descending order. Each one of Pi is done as D+=H, swap, D=H-D, giving exactly a interchanges. This matches 1375-1446.

Covers the cyclic row split into W streams of volume V/W, Phi_M frames giving H<-H+D on every row, the three-update interchange, s calls, the recurrence F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) with both cases of the geometric sum, and the fixed-tape parking schedule. All as at 1491-1588.
Covers the high digits as a row field of range >=W^k with padding below 2R, base-m pieces summing to O(Ve^tau) via a_j<m and m^k<me, and radix padding with e=O(u). This matches 1649-1734.

Covers the P_M conjugation that needs only invertibility, the inverse child through (-i)^f Z C Z, at most m(m-1)+3m row additions, exactly s_c children on e/m axes, and H_0^{⊗D}=b^D S_D C^{⊗D} S_D with the form of b^D. All match 1835-1940.

Follows the paper step by step: the eight parity updates, packed cyclic shifts that agree with T_0 off the guard set, the bad fraction min{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}}, T_0S_0^{-1} permuting B, the radix-sort repair, and the normalized error terms. S1.5.2 gives only the asymptotic O(V(L^tau+1)) form of the time bound, which the lemma also asserts.

Covers the q_0 row chunks, a whole row per role giving exact V/W children, F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), internal costs O(e^lambda), leaves e^sigma d^{(1-sigma)/2}, and the base-m pieces summing to O(d^{lambda'}). All as at 2306-2441.

States the layer with K=floor(d^c), d=Theta(p^eps), O(Vd^{lambda'}) and error below sqrt2·2^{-p}. Derives the guard width (A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E, E=64(W+m+1)^3, m^10<B<m^11, Delta=ceil(C_0 d^20)=o(p)) and the single truncation, as the paper does.

Covers character cancellation through no two-torsion, the DIF recursion, bit-reversed stored order with its reverse procedure, round grouping into H followed by J_E, the layout costs O(TpdK) and O(Tp pK^{tau-1}), layer rounds O(Tp ell d^{lambda'}), commuting truncation past J_E, and the error sqrt2·ell·2^{-p}. All match the paper.
Covers evaluation at B_0=2^{4p}, four products with the established multiplier, the separation |h_j|<=r2^{2p}<B_0/2, centered-residue extraction with carries, and cost O(rp log(rp)), as at 3233-3366.
Covers the retained LB order with P(LBu,LBv)=LB P(u,v), the normalization giving (f*g)/(rM), and error accounting 2delta+eta+delta scaled by M to sqrt2·M(3ell+1)2^{-p}, as at 3414-3478.

Covers the HvdH identity, N=CTD with ||N-I||<1/2, A=S/2 and B_0=2^{-(2alpha^2-2)}D(N^{-1}/2)C with a left inverse, both permutations left unexecuted, the tensor identity with gamma=2d·alpha^2, error dp^2, and the axis-exposure cost O(Tpd^2(1+ell^tau)). All match the paper.

Both identities are stated exactly, with the key reasons (Q reads frequency -s_i j_i; t_i a unit mod s_i, so RF^+R=F^+; the two normalizations). They appear as single infer steps without a method, so they count as stated.
Gives all fixed exponents, the sizes, Rosser-Schoenfeld prime intervals with eta=1/(4d), T/2<S<T, alpha^4 theta_i>3db>=p, and trial division in n^{o(1)}, as in the paper.

Covers the isomorphism argument, the triangular formula b_i, updates in order i=d..1 with valid-interval rotation preserving the zero padding, prefix-controlled shifts, and O(d^2) axis exchanges. Matches 4216-4291.

Covers the source transform composed of A~, the chirp transform through the twist, B~_0 and 2^gamma, its conjugate, and the six-step algorithm with the two S scalings explained by (u*v)/S^2. S3.10 leaves out the 2^{-b-2} input scaling (see errors).
The error chain matches 4583-4727: E_ring<5TL, a .701 margin, chirp <8TL, E_s=9·2^gamma TL, E_w<28·2^gamma T^2L, then 448b·2^{-3b/4}<1/2. It ends with rounding and carry propagation.

Gives V=Tp, the seven margins with min g_2=2^{-181}=2kappa, the source of g_2 (chunk exchanges pK^{tau-1}), o(V) setup and exceptional sorting, log powers absorbed by p^kappa, and the schoolbook cutoff. The seven normalized cost rows are not listed one by one, but their margins are.
Correctly states that T_A(n)/(n lg n)->0 rules out the eventual c_A n lg n lower bound, as at 379-387.

errors.says: Every nonzero edge residual contains a vector of norm one, 'so it is nondegenerate and nonalternating'.
errors.paper: The norm-one vector makes the residual nonalternating. Nondegeneracy comes separately from the orthogonal decompositions ('Each residual is nondegenerate by the decompositions above'). Both are needed for the orthonormal basis.

errors.says: Takes u=Phi(digits) and says scaling by 2^{2b+4}S gives 2^{2b+4}(u*v), whose Phi^{-1} image is the integer digit convolution.
errors.paper: The digits enter scaled by 2^{-b-2} (numerator a_j 2^{p-b-2}), and the factor 2^{2b+4} 'reverses the two input scales'. Without that scaling, 2^{2b+4}(u*v) would not be the integer convolution.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route all the way to the main bound. The network saving s<Wm gives s/W<m^tau. It feeds the interchange recurrence and the layer recurrence, those give the two fast tape procedures, and the procedures feed the synthetic transforms, the convolution, resampling, chirp, CRT, exact recovery and the cost table, whose margin min g_i=2kappa gives O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}). It is thinnest in two places. The label construction asserts the lemma that the only decreasing edges are central 3->4, without the gate-label table. The complex endpoint identity names its Z and i^{27f} corrections without the U_a computation that requires them.

steps.note: The fixed network is reconstructed: the eight-row schedule on triples of [100], the exchange (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) and the restoration of every auxiliary wire. Two pieces are only implicit: N=binom(h,3)^3 (named only as the number of bank values and the total of the source dimensions) and the indexing a in T^3.
A common frame commutes with a pointwise gate, the network implements D_out S D_in^{-1}, and the intermediate frames are free so each edge costs only its frame change.

Labels are nondegenerate subspaces of F^{⊗3} of dimension m, every edge is nested, and the only decreasing edges are the central wires from time 3 to 4, each losing h=100. The gate-label table itself is not given, but the defining claim is.
rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U for nested labels, plus the N exceptional source edges 2P_{U_a} of rank one.
Sum of |Δdim| = Wm-2N+2L by telescoping; L is h times the number of central wires (=Ich); s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.
Gives L/N=100/539 and 101/539, below 1/2, so the deficit N-2L_b>0 (and 2N-2L_c>0) and s<Wm.
M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m with P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m on X_a. Through Phi_M frames this gives H<-H+D on every role, scratch included.
A rank-a shear factors as E_1 Pi E_2 and costs exactly a interchanges plus O(V), so a node makes exactly s recursive calls.
Children have volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), and s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50} from the deficits above 20·2^{-50} and log m<20, giving F_k=O(e^tau).

central.summary: The plan reconstructs all nine steps of the central saving in order. It goes from the scratch-restoring bank exchange, through frames, subspace labels, rank equal to dimension change, the budget W m-N+2L with L/N<1/2, and the endpoint identity, to edges as recursive calls and the recurrence with tau=1-2^{-50}. The only gaps are explicit numerical definitions (N=binom(100,3)^3, indexing by triples of triples) and the gate-label table behind C3.
